segmentation.text: Where the signal is a green turn arrow alone:
until permitted to proceed by another device

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, circular_yellow, circular_red, green_arrow(dir), ...} with dir ∈ {left, right, straight, u_turn}; several states may be displayed at once': a green turn arrow alone is the head displaying green_arrow with direction left, right or u_turn and no state other than green turn arrows (no circular indication, no straight arrow, no yellow, red or flashing arrow). Same words, same atom as the index (NRS_484B_307_4a_o1, NRS_484B_307_4a_o2).

The admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), claimed as ru.aggregate ('membership of a legal aggregate') and never replaced by the class atom ru.pedestrian.

'facing such a signal': the head of s1, at its position (dev.position, 'location of the device head / sign face'), lies within p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach of the pedestrian's position (kin.position, 'position of the body's reference point'), and the pedestrian's heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') makes with the line from its position to the head an angle whose cosine is at least p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos. Not a stand-in: dev.position is read as the place of the head only, never as a stop line or crossing ('the distance to a signal head is a different quantity'). The head is tied to the subject's scene not by this comparison but by the highway of s4, which the head controls.

'the highway' is the definite highway: the one at which 'such a signal' stands and whose traffic it controls. The head controls a junction x (st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'): it governs x itself (dev.governs, 'an intersection, read as control of the junction itself'), or it governs a carrier l (st.travel_region, the abstract kind of every region a device can govern) that runs into x (st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'). 'The highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority') is each way w (st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders') on which x lies (st.on_way, 'an intersection lies on every way that meets there'): the device of the junction is tied to its ways by relation atoms, never by distance. 'shall not enter': the pedestrian's footprint comes to overlap (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a roadway (st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder') lying on w (st.on_way), having overlapped none at the previous observation. The pedestrian who faces the head from the sidewalk or the curb already lies within the highway's width, so the only entry the words can forbid is the step onto its roadway (narrowing on s4); st.roadway's exclusion ('Not a stand-in for: the sidewalk') is the distinction wanted.

'until permitted to proceed by another device': the other device is a pedestrian signal (dev.pedestrian_signal, 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}; countdown attribute when a timer is displayed'), the device of NRS 484B.283(1)(d) that s6 names. It permits the subject to proceed where it shows walk ('While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway', 1d1) or dont_walk_flashing with its countdown attribute ('is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer, a pedestrian may proceed across the highway', 1d2); dont_walk_flashing without countdown and dont_walk_steady permit nothing ('a pedestrian may not proceed to cross the highway', 1d3, 1d4), nor does a dark head. 'Pedestrians facing the signal' is read as the accepted NRS_484B_283_1d1 reads it: the head's position (dev.position) within p.ped_signal_facing_reach of the subject's position (kin.position) and the subject's heading (kin.heading) within the angle whose cosine is p.ped_signal_facing_cos of the line to it. 'proceed across the highway' ties the permitting head to the place entered: it governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — a lane, ... roadway') the roadway the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), or a lane (st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway') lying on the same highway (st.on_way) that its footprint overlaps; the anchor the accepted 1d1 node uses ('a roadway or lane r governed by d'). The permission is a state of the device read directly: no node of NRS 484B.283 states it as the pedestrian's own rule (1d1's node judges the drivers who must yield), so it is read here from the device. Same atoms as the index for 'unless permitted to proceed by another device' (NRS_484B_307_9c), with st.on_way tying the lane to the highway of s4.

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian). At the judged observation there are a traffic signal head s (dev.traffic_signal), an intersection x (st.intersection) and a highway w (st.highway) such that: the subject faces s — s's position (dev.position) lies within p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach of the subject's position (kin.position), and the cosine of the angle between the subject's heading (kin.heading) and the line from its position to s is at least p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos; s displays a green turn arrow alone (green_arrow with direction left, right or u_turn, and no state other than green turn arrows); s controls x: dev.governs(s, x), or dev.governs(s, l) for some travel region l (st.travel_region) with st.lane_enters(l, x); x lies on w (st.on_way(x, w)); and at the previous observation the subject's footprint overlapped (rel.occupies) no roadway r (st.roadway) with st.on_way(r, w). The duty does not apply where NRS_484B_283_1d1, NRS_484B_283_1d2, NRS_484B_283_1d3_o2 or NRS_484B_283_1d4_o2 applies to the subject (ruleApplies, subject mapped to subject): a pedestrian continuing a crossing it entered lawfully under NRS 484B.283.
obligation: For every head s, intersection x and highway w selected again with the applicability's whole selection (the subject faces s as stated there; s displays a green turn arrow alone; s governs x or a travel region that enters x; x lies on w; at the previous observation the subject overlapped no roadway lying on w), and for every roadway r (st.roadway) with st.on_way(r, w): either the subject's footprint does not overlap r (rel.occupies), or the subject is permitted to proceed by a pedestrian signal: there is a pedestrian head d (dev.pedestrian_signal) displaying walk, or displaying dont_walk_flashing with its countdown attribute, that the subject faces and that governs (dev.governs) r itself or a lane l (st.lane) with st.on_way(l, w) whose region the subject's footprint overlaps. The subject faces d where, with Δ the vector from its kin.position to d's dev.position and h its kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach². A head displaying dont_walk_flashing without its countdown, dont_walk_steady or dark permits nothing, and where no pedestrian head is in the scene an entry is violated. Where whether a roadway lies on w, whether the subject overlaps it, or whether a head that would permit is faced or governs the region entered is unobserved and the verdict turns on it, unknown.

narrowings.why: 'enter the highway' is read as coming onto the roadway of a highway on which the junction the signal controls lies (the junction it governs, or the one a carrier it governs enters). The highway's defined extent includes the sidewalk, on which a pedestrian facing the head already stands, so read literally the words would never be engaged by the pedestrians they address; the entry they forbid is the step onto the vehicular part of the highway at that signal. Entry onto a shoulder or verge alone is not read as entry, and a roadway of a way that does not meet at that junction is not 'the highway'. The permission of s5 is read at the observation of the entry: the pedestrian head must then permit, be faced, and govern the roadway entered or a lane of that highway the subject occupies.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian stands on the corner sidewalk of a highway that meets another at a signalized intersection, 25 m from a vehicular head it faces (heading within 10 degrees of the line to the head) that governs a lane entering the intersection and displays green_arrow(left) alone; a pedestrian head 15 m ahead that it faces, governing the roadway it is about to step onto, displays dont_walk_steady. At the next observation its footprint overlaps that roadway, which lies on a highway on which the intersection lies.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the pedestrian stays on the sidewalk while the vehicular head displays green_arrow(left) alone; its footprint never overlaps the roadway.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The vehicular head the pedestrian faces displays circular_green alone; it steps onto the roadway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source supplies no heading for the pedestrian: whether it faces the vehicular head is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the pedestrian head it faces, governing the roadway it steps onto, displays walk at the observation of its entry: another device permits it to proceed.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the roadway the pedestrian steps onto lies on a way that does not meet at the intersection the vehicular head controls (no st.on_way to any highway on which that intersection lies); it never overlaps a roadway of the highway at the signal.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the vehicular head governs the intersection itself (dev.governs on the intersection) rather than an approach lane; the pedestrian steps onto the roadway of a highway on which that intersection lies, its pedestrian head showing dont_walk_steady.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the pedestrian head displays dont_walk_flashing with its countdown attribute at the observation of the entry: the flashing indication with a countdown permits the pedestrian to proceed.

scenarios.name: branch_5
scenarios.narrative: As branch_4, but the pedestrian head displays dont_walk_flashing without a countdown: it permits nothing, and the entry violates the duty. Differs from branch_4 only in the countdown.

scenarios.name: branch_6
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the scene has no pedestrian head at all; the pedestrian steps onto the roadway of the highway at the signal while the vehicular head displays green_arrow(left) alone. The duty binds the subject alone.

scenarios.name: branch_7
scenarios.narrative: As branch_1, but the pedestrian head displaying walk lies behind the pedestrian (the angle between its heading and the line to the head is about 120 degrees): it does not face the device, so it is not permitted, and the entry violates the duty.
